Thanks for the ping, Dylan. I reviewed CareWave's redlines. Key positions and proposed alternatives below (high-level):

1) Custodian / escrow-like mechanism
- CareWave requests an escrow custodian holding a full snapshot. We will not agree to release model weights or keys that enable indefinite redistribution.
- Proposed compromise: "Escrow-lite": Redwood provides encrypted, verifiable snapshots (object manifest + SHA256) to a mutually-agreed third-party custodian under NDA. The custodian stores the encrypted package; Redwood retains the decryption keys in an HSM unless a predefined release condition is met (e.g., provider insolvency or sustained SLA breach).
- Draft language snippet: "In the event of Provider Insolvency or a sustained failure to meet uptime SLA for more than 60 days, Provider shall, upon written request and following validation steps, provide the Customer and the mutually-agreed custodian with an encrypted snapshot and a mechanism for controlled decryption subject to the custodial release protocol."

2) Audit window
- 90-day continuous window is too broad operationally. Acceptable alternative: annual audit with an ad hoc audit window limited to "not to exceed 14 business days" per request and requiring 48 hours' notice; Redwood will provide logs and operator activity relevant to the specific deployment within that window.

3) Operator access & logs
- We can commit to named operator lists and increased logging. Proposed requirement: named operator access plus logs retained for 12 months and exported for audit on request (subject to redaction rules for other customers).

4) License scope
- Insert explicit clause that Customer has a limited license to use the Service for internal production inference only; no redistribution of model weights, and no sublicensing. We will mirror standard Redwood IP protections but add a carve-out for customer-specific fine-tuning outputs if applicable (discuss further).

Next steps: legal will send a redline with the escrow-lite language and the audit limitations. Priyom / Marcus please confirm whether the snapshot + signed manifest approach is workable, and whether the HSM key retention model is feasible operationally (cost/ops implications).

Attachment: RBW_proposed_redlines_CareWave.docx (I will put the draft clauses there).

-laura

Quick operational readout from infra/product:

- Snapshot approach: we can produce an encrypted AMI/container snapshot (or a set of container images + data bundle) and a signed S3 manifest with SHA256 checksums. We can hand that package to a custodian, but we cannot hand over live KMS keys to a third party.
- HSM/KMS model: Redwood can keep the decryption key in our HSM and release it to the custodian only under a controlled protocol. That protocol will require an agreed trigger (bankruptcy/extended SLA breach) and two-step verification (legal signoff + custodian verification).
- Audit logs: we can export operator activity logs and console traces for the requested window. Logs will be redacted to remove other customers' identifiers. Export will take up to 5 business days for a defined window.
- Time/cost: custodial snapshots and restores are operationally heavy. Expect an implementation cost and a one-time fee to set up the custodian flow (we should surface to CareWave). Ongoing custodial storage costs may apply depending on retention.

I attached a short protocol doc for the snapshot/manifest process. Marcus, flag if this is incorrect.
